title: Talent Crunch Hinders SEBI's PMS Global Investment Push
description: SEBI is actively working on regulatory changes to enable Portfolio Management Services (PMS) to offer more international investment opportunities. Indian inve.

faq.a: PMS are professional services offered by investment managers to manage an individual's or institution's investment portfolio. They provide customised investment strategies tailored to the client's financial goals and risk appetite, typically for high-net-worth investors.

faq.q: Why is SEBI encouraging global investments for PMS?
faq.a: SEBI is encouraging global investments to offer Indian investors more avenues for portfolio diversification, reduce concentration risk in domestic markets, and allow access to international growth opportunities and sectors not available locally.

faq.q: How does the talent crunch affect me as an investor?
faq.a: The talent crunch can lead to fewer comprehensive global investment options from PMS providers, potentially higher management fees for international portfolios, or delays in the launch of sophisticated global investment products.

faq.q: Are there existing ways for Indians to invest globally?
faq.a: Yes, Indian investors can currently invest globally through Indian mutual funds with international mandates, Exchange Traded Funds (ETFs) that track global indices, or directly via the Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS) regulated by the RBI.

faq.q: What should I look for in a PMS offering international investments?
faq.a: Look for a PMS with a demonstrable track record in global markets, experienced fund managers with international expertise, robust research capabilities for various geographies, a clear understanding of currency and geopolitical risks, and transparent fee structures.

faq.q: Will global PMS investments be taxed differently?
faq.a: Yes, investments in foreign assets through a PMS will be subject to Indian income tax laws, including capital gains tax, which can vary based on the holding period. It's also crucial to consider tax implications in the foreign jurisdiction and any applicable double taxation avoidance agreements (refer to Income Tax India for details).
